mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates aggressive monetary accommodation that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 4.0% signals labor market tightness that increases corporate profit margins through reduced wage pressures, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and increases in CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicate weakening consumer demand coupled with rising price pressures, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining HOUST and rising CPIAUCSL fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals manufacturing contraction that precedes equity market downturns, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO declines in late-cycle expansion do not lead to negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand for residential construction, which correlates with broader economic expansion and positive equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST increases are followed by negative 5-day SPX returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 1.5% combined with CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 1.5% and CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%
failure_condition: The combined signal of FEDFUNDS>1.5% and CPIAUCSL>2.5% fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) and decline in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates labor market strength without corresponding consumer spending growth, triggering negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling RSAFS does not lead to negative returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In post-shock recovery regimes, a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals improving labor market conditions that boost consumer confidence and spending, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE declines in post-shock recovery periods are followed by negative 5-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases.
